substantive_reconstruction.orthogonal_blocks: Use the orthogonal central Schur-Weyl isotypical projections P_lambda, not unnormalized Young symmetrizers. Positivity of rho tensor n makes each trace nonnegative, and the resolution of identity gives total1. The actual block is I_(V_lambda) tensor omega_lambda(rho), giving w=f_lambda tr omega_lambda(rho). Diagonalizing rho by a unitary does not change these central block weights.
substantive_reconstruction.character_bound: A semistandard tableau of shape lambda has no repeated label in any column. For any k labels, a column of height h holds at most min(k,h) occurrences; summing columns gives lambda1+...+lambdak. Thus sorted content nu^down is majorized by lambda. Rearrangement against decreasing log(s) and summation by parts (prefix differences nonnegative, total difference0) yield s^nu<=s^lambda when s>0. The row-constant tableau contributes s^lambda. The Schur character is consequently between s^lambda and m_lambda*s^lambda. This requires only the valid necessary content restriction and weight basis, not a false fixed-word survival iff.
substantive_reconstruction.padded_hook_lower_bound: Put beta_i=lambda_i+d-i and r=d(d-1)/2. The row-i hook product equals beta_i! divided by product_{j>i}(beta_i-beta_j): row hooks occupy1,...,beta_i with exactly those beta_i-beta_j omitted. Multiplying gives f=n!*product_{i<j}(lambda_i-lambda_j+j-i)/product_i(lambda_i+d-i)!. Each numerator integer is>=1. After dividing out lambda_i!, the denominator has sum_i(d-i)=r extra factors, each<=n+d. Therefore f>=C_lambda/(n+d)^r. Also f<=C_lambda since standard tableaux inject into assignments of the n numbers to increasing rows. Padded zero rows cause no division by zero or factorial defect.
substantive_reconstruction.weyl_upper_bound: Weyl gives m_lambda=product_{i<j}(lambda_i-lambda_j+j-i)/(j-i). Each denominator is a positive integer and each ratio<=n+d (indeed<=n+1), so m_lambda<=(n+d)^r. The f and m factors are not interchanged.
substantive_reconstruction.multinomial_mode_proof: For p_i=lambda_i/n, the type-lambda probability is T_lambda=C_lambda product_i p_i^lambda_i=C_lambda exp(-nH(p)). It is<=1. For any supported type mu of total n, T_mu/T_lambda is product_i lambda_i^(mu_i-lambda_i)*lambda_i!/mu_i!: n factors cancel because sums agree. If mu_i=lambda_i+h, its factor is product_{t=1}^h lambda_i/(lambda_i+t)<=1; if mu_i=lambda_i-h, it is product_{t=0}^{h-1}(lambda_i-t)/lambda_i<=1. Coordinates with lambda_i=0 have mu_i=0 in the supported case and factor1; any mu with positive mass there has probability0. Thus lambda is a mode. There are at most(n+1)^d types of total probability1, so T_lambda>=(n+1)^(-d). This rigorously gives the candidate's upper and lower entropy estimates, not just an asymptotic Stirling assertion.
substantive_reconstruction.finite_n_prefactors: Combining f>=C/(n+d)^r, character>=s^lambda and C>=(n+1)^(-d)exp(nH), then n+1<=n+d, gives w>=(n+d)^(-r-d)exp(-nD). The upper bounds give w<=(n+d)^r exp(-nD). Here r+d=d(d+1)/2, exactly the exponent in step3. For rho=I2/2,n=2,lambda=(2,0), w=3/4 while bare exp(-nD)=1/4, so deleting the factor really is invalid.
substantive_reconstruction.zero_support: If rank(s)=q and lambda has more than q nonzero rows, its first column cannot be strictly filled using only q positive labels; all character monomials vanish, w=0. Since ordered s has zeros beyond q, such p has mass outside support and D=+infinity, so exp(-nD)=0 and both inequalities remain valid. For lambda with at most q rows, the row-constant monomial is positive and the same proof applies on the q-dimensional support, retaining the larger d-dependent bounds. No full-rank premise is inserted.
substantive_reconstruction.union_and_rate_quantifiers: On the closed probability face supported on the q positive eigenvalues, D is continuous even at p_i=0 (x log x extends continuously), nonnegative, and zero only at s. The closed epsilon-complement is compact with strictly positive minimum delta unless empty. Unsupported diagrams already have zero weight. Summing at most(n+1)^d upper bounds gives outside mass<=(n+1)^d(n+d)^r exp(-n delta)->0 for fixed d. This supplies the factor missing from the extracted source Eq9.35. For supported nonzero weights the two-sided bounds give D-r log(n+d)/n <= -log(w)/n <= D+(r+d)log(n+d)/n. Hence along supported p_n->p the rate tends to D(p||s). This does not apply that finite rate to sequences of unsupported outcomes approaching the support.
substantive_reconstruction.boundaries_and_scope: n>=1 is required only for lambda/n; the asymptotic question does not ask n=0. A density state forces d>=1. d=1 has one certain supported outcome; rank1 in any d has only lambda=(n) supported. No constant lower atom probability near s, eventual exact matching diagram, efficient Schur-transform implementation or finite-bit bound is asserted.
